column1: # planning/parity/carriers.tsv — one row per landing that touched ONE router and not the other.
# THE CARRIER IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN HERE AS A CLAIM. It is measured from the landing's own diff by
# scripts/acceptance/carrier-census.sh and this file records what was DECIDED about it. The gate,
# planning/carrier-parity-gate.py, re-measures on every run and reports a row whose recorded
# carrier disagrees with the tree. Editing a carrier cell here changes nothing except whether the
# gate goes red.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `src/*.ts` and `app/Sources/RouterCore` + `app/Sources/MCPRouterCLI` are two
# implementations of one router, and the differential harness compares BEHAVIOUR on rows that exist
# on both. A capability that exists on one side has no row to compare, so the absence and the
# agreement are indistinguishable to every gate in this tree. R33 was filed after a deploy measured
# `GET /caches` answering 404 on the running router while `GET /sessions` answered 200: R28, R30,
# R31 and R32 are Swift-only, R29 is TypeScript-only, all five merged green.
# One-sidedness is NOT a defect and this file never says it is. R4-C1 pointed the installer at
# Swift and held the TypeScript deletion; REQ-020 reserves the retirement to the owner. Building
# where the subject lives is correct. What was missing is that nobody had to say so.
# THE OBLIGATION BEGINS AT THE PIN AND NOT BEFORE. `since` below is the commit from which every
# one-sided landing needs a row. Earlier one-sided landings are counted and printed by the gate as
# a stated backlog, never as a pass and never as an amnesty — the same shape sweep-control-gate.py
# gives its grandfathered set. The pin is the goal that produced the five items R33 measured, so
# the window opens exactly where the divergence it is about begins.
# since: afaad591fcfd6783b2aa706281b390dcabeafe33
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   sha          the full 40-character landing sha. The key. The gate joins on this and nothing else
#   label        the branch or item name, for a reader. Convenience only; the gate ignores it
#   carrier      swift-only | typescript-only — re-measured every run, and a disagreement is a red
#   disposition  divergent-recorded | ported | reference-only | not-a-feature
#   note         why, and what would close it. A row with an empty note is a red
# divergent-recorded  one-sided on purpose; the other implementation does not carry it and nobody
#                     is claiming it does. The note says what the consequence is on a default install
# ported              one-sided landing whose counterpart landed separately; the note names the sha
# reference-only      TypeScript-side work on the harness reference itself, which by definition has
#                     no Swift counterpart
# not-a-feature       a one-sided touch carrying no capability — a rename, a lint fix, a comment

column5: The gap-fix for WIN17's verified NEEDS-WORK: D1 epoch flooring inside PowerShell, D2 async powershell lanes off the event loop, G1 the config-watcher guarantee stated instead of invented, and the parity-vector position. TypeScript-only because every fix is in the node router's Windows arms (src/platform.ts, src/watch.ts, src/index.ts, its harness); the Swift router builds only on macOS and has no Windows surface for these to diverge from, so there is nothing on that side to port and none is claimed. Same direction as rescue-w1: the reference gained Windows correctness the Swift binary cannot carry while it remains macOS-only. Repointed 2026-08-31 from the branch tip to the landing merge 177a416d, per the r22 row's recorded convention. Repointed 2026-10-19: z13 committed this as 177a416d and never pushed; it reached this branch's first parent inside 6facb8e2, the merge of z13's main, which carries no other router change.

column1: a0dfd38162acddc8e21ae9b329aae08fbe83bc73
column5: A complexity refactor of RouterCore/Control/ControlHandler.swift (19+/7-): route reading restructured, no behaviour added or removed. Swift-only because the file is Swift; the TypeScript reference's control handler in src/control.ts was not touched by the landing and needed nothing - there is no feature on either side to diverge, which is why this is not-a-feature rather than divergent-recorded. Recorded rather than skipped because the census measures the landing as one-sided and this file records what was DECIDED about that.

W1's recovered work plus the Windows verification lane: src/platform.ts's win32 arms, scripts/windows/verify.ps1, scripts/e2e-platform.mjs, and sessions/usage/lock/watch corrections. TypeScript-only because the Swift router has no Windows surface and builds only on macOS - there is no counterpart to diverge from and none is claimed; the node router gained Windows portability the Swift binary cannot have while it remains macOS-only (R4/REQ-020 reserve that decision for the owner). Not a waiver: the divergence direction is that the reference gained a platform the Swift implementation deliberately lacks, and that is recorded here rather than silently absorbed.

The extension store. 12 files under RouterCore/MCPRouterCLI, no TypeScript counterpart. Reachable only on an install that selected the Swift binary; `MCPR_ROUTER="${MCPR_ROUTER:-swift}"`, `docs/install.sh:39` at `83e5380`, has defaulted to swift since R4-C1, so a FRESH install carries it and an install predating R4-C1 does not. Closed by REQ-020's cutover, which is the owner's, or by a port nobody has proposed.

Session push and live tool-list reload. 6 files under src/, no Swift counterpart. This is the inverse case and the one that made the gap visible: on a default install (swift) it is the four Swift items that answer and R29 that does not, and the deploy R33 was filed from measured the opposite because those launchd agents still ran node. Which router answers is a property of the INSTALL, not of this repository, and this file does not pretend to know it.

Ingest — copy-verify-remove of what Claude acquires, reversibly. 16 files under RouterCore/Extensions and MCPRouterCLI. Landed as a SINGLE-PARENT commit whose subject reads `Merge ai/r30`, which is why the census walks first-parent rather than `--merges`: a merge-only walk does not select it and would have missed a quarter of R33's own subject.

Cache invalidation — the content component beside the identity key. 14 files under RouterCore. `GET /caches` is the route the deploy measured answering 404 on the running node router; the 404 is correct for that binary, because the route exists only in Swift.

The Desktop entry and its person-driven reload. 6 files under RouterCore. Same shape as R28 and R31: reachable on a Swift install, absent on a node one, and no claim is made that the reference carries it.

Upstream health probing and its two routes. 11 files under RouterCore, no TypeScript counterpart: src/control.ts answers /upstreams/health 404 and falls through to its own 405 on /servers/:name/probe, which is what makes the div-r27-* rows proven-by-suite rather than proven — there is nothing to diff bytes against and two routers being equally silent is not agreement. Same shape as R28, R31 and R32: reachable on an install that selected the Swift binary, absent on a node one, and no claim is made about which is installed on a given machine. What would close it is a port of the health module into src/, which nobody is asking for while REQ-020 reserves the cutover to the owner.

Invocation history and the version boundary set. 15 files under RouterCore/Invocations plus one path accessor on UpstreamConfig, no TypeScript counterpart and none owed: src/*.ts has no extension store, no transcript reader and no notion of a capability version, so there is nothing on that side for a differential harness to compare. Same shape as R28, R30, R31 and R32 — reachable on an install that selected the Swift binary, absent on a node one, and no claim is made about which is installed on a given machine. What is NOT the reason: this is not a Swift-only surface because porting was hard. The subject is a corpus of harness session transcripts under a root the operator names, and the node router has no configuration that could point at one.

GET /invocations and GET /invocations/export, plus their suites. 4 files under RouterCore/Control and app/Tests. src/control.ts answers both paths 404, which is exactly why the two div-f5-* rows in surface.tsv carry proven-by-suite rather than proven: there is nothing to diff bytes against and two routers being equally silent is not agreement. Identical in shape to div-r28-* and div-r27-*, and the honest reading is that a node install serves no invocation history at all rather than an empty one.

Two doc comments under RouterCore gained the tree their citation into the design of record was missing. Swift-only because the files are Swift; nothing about the router's behaviour moved on either side, and the TypeScript reference has no counterpart to these comments because it has no invocation history to comment on. Recorded rather than waved through: this gate reports one-sidedness and does not judge it, and a landing whose whole content is prose is still a landing that touched one implementation.

The daemon's supply of the invocation reporter, plus InvocationSources. 3 files under RouterCore and app/Tests. Swift-only for the same reason f5-core is, one level sharper: MCP_ROUTER_TRANSCRIPTS points the reader at a corpus of harness session transcripts, and src/*.ts has no configuration surface that could hold such a root, no reader to hand it to, and no route that would answer for it. Same shape as R28, R30, R31 and R32 — reachable on an install that selected the Swift binary, absent on a node one.

The once-per-start corpus scan, detached after listen(). 1 file under RouterCore/Service. Swift-only for the reason f5-wiring is: there is no corpus, no reader and no configuration on the TypeScript side to arm. Recorded as its own row rather than folded into f5-wiring because the census walks FIRST-PARENT commits and disposition is per landing — the two are one decision and two landings, and a gate that let one row speak for two would let a later landing hide behind an earlier one.

The window's accounting, corrected to report the scan's figures rather than the invocation log's. 2 files under RouterCore/Invocations and app/Tests. Swift-only for the reason f5-core is: the reference has no transcript reader whose reach there would be anything to report about. Worth a row of its own rather than a fold into f5-core because the defect it fixes is one the reference cannot have and a reader comparing the two implementations should not go looking for it there.

Seeding the version boundary set from Claude's plugin register before the first scan, plus its suite. 4 files under RouterCore and app/Tests. Swift-only for the reason f5-wiring is: src/*.ts has no ledger to seed, no reader to seed it for, and no route that would answer from it. The register it reads is Claude's own installed_plugins.json, which R30 already reads on the Swift side and which the reference has never read at all.

The diagnostics bundle and its redactor. 8 files under RouterCore and RouterCoreTests, no TypeScript counterpart: src/control.ts claims neither /diagnostics nor /diagnostics/bundle in its isControlPath, so both fall through to /mcp and answer 404, which is what makes the div-r22-* rows proven-by-suite rather than proven - there is nothing to diff bytes against and two routers being equally silent is not agreement. Same shape as R27, R28, R31 and R32: reachable on an install that selected the Swift binary, absent on a node one, and no claim is made about which is installed on a given machine. WHAT THIS ONE COSTS ON A NODE INSTALL IS WORTH NAMING RATHER THAN LEAVING TO THE SHAPE: the operator gets no export at all, which is a missing convenience - they do NOT get an unredacted one, because the reference has no such route to answer badly. So the divergence withholds a feature and never a guarantee, and that is the direction that makes it safe to leave open. What would close it is a port of RouterCore/Diagnostics into src/ plus the two routes, which nobody is asking for while REQ-020 reserves the cutover to the owner. REPOINTED 2026-08-31 from the branch tip to the merge that landed it on main's first-parent line, which is what the census walks.

The update check and its route. 13 files under RouterCore, no TypeScript counterpart: src/control.ts answers /extensions/updates 404, exactly as it answers every path under /extensions (R28) and /caches (R31), so there is no reference behaviour to port and none is claimed. Declared as div-f6-updates in planning/parity/surface.tsv with the verdict word proven-by-suite rather than proven, because no lane drives the reference against it - two routers being equally silent is not agreement. The reason this landing is one-sided is the same as R28's and R31's and it is structural rather than a scheduling accident: the router this route reads is the SWIFT store at <router home>/extensions, which the node router has no concept of, so a TypeScript half would have nothing to read. What a node install gets instead is a 404, and that is the honest answer for a router that holds no extensions rather than a gap to be filled.

The session analyst PRD.md §6 specifies, and the three control arms that serve it. 20 files under RouterCore/Analyst, RouterCore/Control, MCPRouterKit and MCPRouterUI, no TypeScript counterpart. Same shape as R27, R28, R31 and R32, and one degree stronger: `src/control.ts` answers the whole `/insights` family 404 by design (`div-m22-insights`), so this item adds two sub-paths to a route the reference has never served and never will — there is nothing to diff bytes against, and two routers being equally silent is not agreement. What would close it is a port of the analyst into `src/`, which nobody is asking for while REQ-020 reserves the cutover to the owner. It would also need a JSONL reader over the caller's own session stores and a child-process judge inside the node router, which is a larger surface than the route. ROW REPOINTED 2026-08-31: the census walks main's first-parent line, where this landing is the integ/n34 merge (which also carried F8's Swift profiles store — one one-sided landing, one row). The old sha was the branch tip and joins to nothing on that line.

Stdio entries take envFile, and the router loads .env then .env.local from the package root at every spawn (src/envfile.ts, src/config.ts, src/pool.ts). The commit measures dossier's four paid backends reading no credentials without it. No Swift counterpart: a grep for .env, .env.local, dotenv and envFile in app/Sources/RouterCore and app/Sources/MCPRouterCLI is empty. On a default install (swift) a stdio server whose keys sit only in its package .env.local gets none from the router. Closed by REQ-020's cutover, which is the owner's, or by a port nobody has proposed.

Two reference changes. Each entry carries a size-and-mtime stamp of its executable, so a replaced binary is re-read (src/config.ts, src/manifest.ts). The router injects the caller's project into a tool's project argument where the tool declares one (src/router.ts withCallerProject). No Swift counterpart: UpstreamHash folds no executable stamp into the identity, and a grep for callerProject and withCallerProject in RouterCore and MCPRouterCLI is empty. Whether a replaced binary goes stale on a default swift install is not measured here. Closed by REQ-020's cutover, which is the owner's, or by a port nobody has proposed.

column1: f955841af9efbffb16fef228c5a21cda4d3cbbbb
column5: R26's router half: GET /upstreams/auth-expiry, POST /upstreams/auth-expiry/notify, and an expiry monitor and policy under RouterCore/AuthExpiry. The reference already derives the same expiry (src/auth.ts tokenExpiry, read into an upstream's listing reason at src/oauth.ts:333), but it has no monitor, no notice and no auth-expiry route: a grep for auth-expiry and expiry in src/control.ts, src/router.ts and src/livereload.ts is empty. The desktop delivery, click-through and indicator are R26-C1 and are not in this landing. Closed by REQ-020's cutover, which is the owner's, or by a port nobody has proposed.

The reference's first tests: test/binary-stamp, test/envfile and test/router-project, with tsconfig.test.json, a package.json script and a .gitignore entry. It also moves the caller-project injection out of buildMcpServer into withCallerProject in src/router.ts, keeping the same conditions, so the injection can be tested without a server. The harness drives the reference, so tests of it have no Swift counterpart.
